items.stem: In Java, what precisely is a data race?

options.text: Two or more threads access the same memory concurrently, at least one writes, and there is no synchronisation
options.rationale: Correct: that unsynchronised concurrent access with a writer is the definition of a data race.

options.text: Any program that uses more than one thread
options.rationale: Multithreading alone is not a data race.

options.text: A loop that iterates faster than expected
options.rationale: Loop speed is unrelated to data races.

options.text: Two functions defined with the same name
options.rationale: Naming collisions are a different concern.

items.explanation: Correct: that unsynchronised concurrent access with a writer is the definition of a data race.

items.stem: Which TWO practices genuinely help performance in Java? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Profiling first to find the real bottleneck before changing code
options.rationale: Correct: measurement directs effort to where it matters.

options.text: Reducing unnecessary allocations in a hot path
options.rationale: Correct: fewer allocations cut memory pressure and overhead in hot code.

options.text: Rewriting every loop by hand before measuring anything
options.rationale: Premature optimisation wastes effort and can add bugs.

options.text: Adding threads to code that is bound by a single shared lock
options.rationale: Contention on one lock means more threads will not help.

items.explanation: Correct: measurement directs effort to where it matters.

items.stem: A Java codebase applies the Singleton pattern to almost every class. What is the main risk?

options.text: Hidden global state and tight coupling that make the code hard to test and change
options.rationale: Correct: overusing singletons reintroduces global state and coupling.
Overuse is a design problem, not a compile error.

options.text: The pattern makes all code automatically thread-safe
Patterns can only be used once per program

items.explanation: Correct: overusing singletons reintroduces global state and coupling.
